summary: Discovery focused on security posture for potentially using Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Cypher Health is highly security conscious (healthcare/PHI) and needs SOC 2/ISO artifacts, SAML SSO, RBAC, tenant isolation, audit logs, and KMS integration. Discussion covered encryption at-rest/in-transit, key management options, data retention and deletion, and compliance timelines. Agreed next steps: Redwood to share certs and runbook; schedule SE-led deep dive and benchmarks.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment tradeoffs
transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-03-24 15:30 PDT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Priya (CS), Anita (CISO, Cypher), Roberto (VP Eng), Ethan (Infra), Sofia (Legal, left early)

Summary: quick intro, then deep into security requirements. Transcript below likely has some auto-transcription noise.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone thanks for joining, this is Maya from Redwood Inference, i'm here with Liam our solutions engineer, and Priya from CS will pop in at the end. How are you all?
[00:06] Anita: Hi, thanks. This is Anita, CISO at Cypher Health, we brought Roberto and Ethan. Sofia from legal will sit in first 10 minutes.
[00:11] Roberto: Hey all.
[00:13] Liam: Great, thanks. High level -- we want to understand your security bar and whether Hosted, Dedicated, or Private makes sense. We'll cover certs, SSO, KMS, logs, retention.
[00:20] Anita: Yeah main points: we handle PHI, so need SOC 2 type II, ISO 27001, SAML SSO (IdP is Okta), SCIM for provisioning, strong RBAC, full audit logs, immutable audit trail, encryption keys managed by our KMS (AWS KMS / HSM), and clear data retention / deletion SLAs.
[00:36] Maya: Understood. We support SSO via SAML and OIDC, SCIM for user sync, RBAC with per-team and per-role controls. For keys, we have KMS integrations for Dedicated and Private -- hosted customers can bring keys via BYOK for some plans; i'll let Liam detail.
[00:49] Liam: Quick note: Hosted has tenant isolation and encryption at rest, but persistent key ownership is limited for lower tiers. Dedicated gives you isolated GPU pools and we can integrate with your KMS using an external key wrapper or HSM via customer-managed VPC. Private gives you full control -- private control plane, you manage KMS/HSM, network egress rules.
[01:12] Sofia (softly): legal question on subprocessor list and data residency?
[01:16] Maya: yes we'll send our subprocessor list and data residency doc. We have EU region options and contractual terms.
[01:22] Anita: How is audit logging surfaced? We need immutable logs, long retention, and the ability to push to our SIEM (Splunk).
[01:30] Liam: Logs: we emit detailed audit events -- per-request metadata, actor, model/version, latency, tokens -- and we can stream logs to customers via secure syslog or Kinesis or S3 ingestion. For Hosted we retain logs by default for X days, but retention policies can be extended as an add-on. For Dedicated/Private, retention and export are in your control; hooks to your SIEM are standard.
[01:52] Ethan: When you say per-request metadata, does that include prompt content? That's a big no for PHI unless customer opts in.
[02:00] Maya: Good callout. By default we redwood redact certain PII in telemetry; we also have options to disable prompt logging -- especially for Private. We treat "prompt content" as sensitive and have policies and scrubbers, but need to work out specifics with security teams.
[02:18] Anita: Encryption -- we need customer-managed keys for at-rest data (models, KV cache, logs) and TLS in transit. Can Redwood integrate with our AWS KMS CMKs or an HSM backed key?
[02:28] Liam: Yes. For Dedicated and Private we support EKM/HSM and can configure envelope encryption where the data key is wrapped by your CMK. For Hosted customers we offer BYOK where feasible but certain hosted flows use service-managed keys. We'll attach a note in the docs about which endpoints use which key types.
[02:46] Roberto: Latency tradeoffs -- if we use Private with on-prem, we might see improved latency but more ops. For Hosted, what's the SLA and region placement?
[02:55] Maya: Hosted has multi-region endpoints, SLA varies by plan; Dedicated has SLA-backed latency and throughput. Private you can colocate in-region or on-prem for lowest latency but requires customer infra. We'll provide a latency/throughput benchmark baseline.
[03:08] Anita: Compliance artifacts -- we need SOC 2 type II, ISO 27001, penetration test reports, and a signed DPA.
[03:15] Maya: We'll send SOC2 and ISO certs and our standard DPA -- action item.
[03:19] Liam: Also note our security whitepaper covers certs and pentest cadence.
[03:25] [03:25] (crosstalk) Sofia: also want vendor risk questionnaire answers -- can you fill out our VRF?
[03:30] Maya: yes we can -- small teams usually have a prefilled VRF; larger questionnaires we'll ask for template.
[03:34] Ethan: Regarding RBAC -- do you support attribute-based access or mapping to Okta groups via SCIM so engineers only see models relevant to them?
[03:43] Liam: We support roles and teams out of the box, and SCIM can sync groups. We map SAML assertions to roles and have can policies. We also integrate with your IdP for session duration, MFA enforcement and SSO.
[03:57] Anita: Data retention -- we need 90 day hot retention for logs, 7-year legal retention for certain audit events, and automated deletion for prompt data within 30 days unless flagged. Is that configurable?
[04:10] Liam: Yes -- for Dedicated and Private you can configure retention windows and export to cold storage. For Hosted it's configurable via add-on and we can support custom retention SLAs with a contract.
[04:22] Roberto: Is there a way to opt-out of model telemetry entirely? We don't want any prompt or output stored outside our control.
[04:29] Maya: We have a strict telemetry policy and more restrictive settings for enterprise customers. Private deployment gives you complete control; Dedicated can be configured to minimize telemetry and ship logs to your systems. Hosted default retains some telemetry for troubleshooting unless a contractual requirement is made.
[04:46] [05:00] Liam: Back to KMS -- we'll need a network path from the runtime to your KMS for envelope decryption. For cloud KMS this is typically over private VPC endpoints. For on-prem HSMs we do an offline key-wrapping step. We'll capture the details in the runbook.
[05:18] Anita: Can you provide an architecture diagram showing where model weights, kv cache, and logs are stored and encrypted?
[05:24] Liam: Absolutely. We'll attach an architecture diagram and a data flow chart in the runbook.
[05:29] Sofia: Any subprocessor changes require 30 day notification in contract?
[05:32] Maya: We'll confirm the notice period in the DPA.
[05:36] Anita: Pen tests -- do you do third-party pen tests and can we get summaries?
[05:41] Liam: We do yearly third-party pentests and will share executive summaries. Full reports can be shared under NDA.
[05:48] Roberto: Are there any OpenAI or Anthropic model dependencies? We saw competitor references earlier -- curious if any third party model calls are made.
[05:57] Maya: We host and curate model catalog; some customer workflows might call external APIs but Redwood's hosted inference runs on the model binaries we serve. We can restrict any external calls.
[06:07] Ethan: Network egress -- we need explicit egress controls and restricted outbound traffic.
[06:12] Liam: For Dedicated/Private you control egress rules via VPC configs. For Hosted we have egress controls and can route through customer proxies via peering for enterprise.
[06:22] Anita: Ok this is good. Can you outline the differences again succinctly?
[06:26] Maya: Short: Hosted = fastest time-to-value, managed keys/service-managed encryption, reasonable telemetry; Dedicated = reserved capacity, isolated tenant resources, customer key integrations, SLA; Private = customer-run control plane, full KMS/HSM, on-prem/VPC deployment, maximal data control.
[06:43] [06:43] (small pause)
[06:47] Roberto: For our pilot we want to start with Dedicated in our AWS account with customer KMS and SIEM integration, then consider Private if ops cost is OK. Timeline target: pilot in Q2, production Q3.
[06:59] Maya: That works, we'll follow up with pricing and a benchmark plan.
[07:03] Liam: We'll want to run token/latency benchmarks with representative prompts and payload sizes; recommended to run 24-72 hour sustained tests to catch batching behaviors.
[07:14] Ethan: We'll provide sample prompt set and typical seq lengths.
[07:18] Maya: Great. Any final legal items Sofia?
[07:21] Sofia: No, we'll wait for DPA and certs.
[07:24] Maya: ok recap -- action items: send SOC2/ISO, send runbook + arch diagram, prepare benchmark plan, customer to share network/KMS diagrams and retention reqs. We'll schedule the SE deep dive for next week.
[07:37] Anita: Thanks everyone.
[07:39] Maya: Thanks, we'll follow up via email.

Notes about transcript: timestamps are approximate; occasional transcription errors (Redwood product names appear as "red wood" or "red wood inference") and some spec names slightly mis-spelled.

End of call.
